subject: medicine
title: Rheumatoid arthritis: symmetric erosive polyarthritis

steps.tx: People with **rheumatoid arthritis** often report symmetric pain and swelling in the small joints of the hands and feet while the distal interphalangeal joints stay spared. Morning **stiffness** lasts well over an hour and eases with gentle movement during the day. Ask about swan neck and boutonniere shapes, drifting of the fingers, rheumatoid **nodules** over pressure areas, neck pain with weakness or clumsiness, dry eyes and dry mouth, breathlessness with cough, smoking history and regular medicines.
steps.say: Rheumatoid arthritis usually causes symmetric pain and swelling in the small joints of the hands and feet, and the end joints of the fingers often stay spared. Morning stiffness often lasts beyond one hour and then eases as the person keeps moving through the day. Ask about finger drift and bent shapes, lumps over pressure areas, neck pain with weakness, dry eyes with dry mouth, cough with breathlessness, smoking history and current medicines.

steps.tx: On examination look for symmetric swelling of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints with sparing of the distal joints. Note ulnar **drift** with volar subluxation, swan neck hyperextension, boutonniere flexion and **Z thumb** deformity in established disease. Feel for rheumatoid **nodules** at the elbow and Achilles tendon, test grip strength, squeeze across the knuckles for tenderness, check the neck for instability, look at the eyes and inspect leg ulcers and nailfold lesions.
steps.say: On examination the knuckle joints often look swollen and tender in a symmetric pattern, and the end joints usually stay spared. Established disease shows finger drift with sliding tendons, swan neck extension with boutonniere bending, and thumb collapse that limits pinch. Feel for firm lumps at the elbow, test grip strength, squeeze the knuckles gently, check neck movement with neurology, look at the eyes, and inspect the skin for ulcers.

steps.tx: Blood tests show a raised C reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate with disease activity, while **anti CCP** antibodies support early rheumatoid arthritis and **rheumatoid factor** supports seropositive disease. Plain **radiographs** of the hands show periarticular osteopenia with marginal erosions and symmetric narrowing, and ultrasound with Doppler shows active synovitis. Consider neck flexion views when instability is suspected, arrange eye review for scleritis, and compare against psoriatic arthritis, lupus, gout and septic arthritis.
steps.say: Blood tests often show raised inflammatory markers that rise and fall with disease activity, and antibody tests support early and seropositive disease. Hand radiographs often show soft bone loss near joints with small edge erosions and even narrowing across joints, and Doppler ultrasound shows active joint inflammation. Ask for neck views when the neck feels unstable, arrange an eye review for redness and pain, and keep psoriasis with nail disease, lupus without erosions, gout and joint infection in mind.

steps.tx: This bilateral hand radiograph shows the classic rheumatoid pattern that supports the bedside diagnosis. Periarticular **osteopenia** appears as paler bone beside the small joints, while the arrows mark small marginal **erosions** at the metacarpophalangeal joints. Symmetric joint space **narrowing** affects the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints, and the changes match on both hands. Correlate the picture with swelling, morning stiffness and antibody results before confirming the diagnosis.
steps.say: This hand radiograph shows pale bone near the small joints, small edge erosions at the knuckles, and even narrowing that looks the same on both hands. The arrows indicate marginal erosions with soft bone loss and joint space loss at the knuckle and finger joints. Use the picture with swelling on examination, prolonged morning stiffness, and antibody results to support the diagnosis and to explain joint damage to the patient.

steps.tx: Start **methotrexate** as the anchor disease modifying drug with folate cover, blood counts, liver tests and chest vigilance, and use a short steroid bridge with calcium and bone protection. Step up to **biologic** therapy or a targeted synthetic drug when methotrexate alone fails to control activity. Add physiotherapy with splints and grip aids, use killed vaccines before immune suppression, stop methotrexate and leflunomide before **pregnancy**, guard the unstable neck during anaesthesia, pause immune drugs during infection and track activity with joint counts and inflammatory markers.
steps.say: Treatment usually starts with methotrexate with folate cover and careful blood, liver and lung checks, and a short steroid bridge protects joints while it takes effect. When control stays poor, the team steps up to biologic treatment or a targeted tablet with vaccine and infection planning. Add hand therapy with splints, guard the neck during procedures, pause immune drugs during fever, avoid harmful drugs in pregnancy, and track swelling with blood markers and joint counts.
